Bonus · one ranking across every version

near-identical snippets collapsed to one row
The brief names the difficulty itself: across versions the snippets “would still be very similar, which would make them hard to rank properly”. Searching every snapshot naively makes it worse — a function that survived four commits returns four near-identical rows and crowds the rest out. Rows are grouped by the identity that survives a commit (path + symbol), each collapsing to its best-scoring variant. The right-hand column is the ungrouped ranking, so the difference is measured rather than claimed.

What produced it

Three passes over CoIR AppsRetrieval: a dense pass with the published F2LLM-v2 recipe, a lexical pass, and an execution pass that runs the top-20 candidates against the worked examples parsed out of the problem statement and promotes whichever ones reproduce them. The execution pass is the only one that cleared a paired bootstrap gate — the nine-feature reranker did not, and ships as the identity configuration rather than being quietly left in.

The same three passes answer the queries on the Retrieve tab. What changes there is the corpus: a repository has no worked examples to run, so the execution pass reports that it had nothing to execute instead of showing a badge it did not earn.
